newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Stockpile to open germanium bid March 24.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Stockpile to open germanium bid March 24.

text.p: The Defense National Stockpile Center said it will open its first sale of surplus germanium metal on March 24 when 4,000 kilograms will be on the block.

The stockpile has authority to sell 4,000 kilos this fiscal year which ends on September 30, and if all the material is not sold in March, the balance will be offered on the fourth Monday of each month until exhausted.

However Richard Connelly, stockpile administrator, told a meeting of germanium officials called by the DNSC here that he fully expected an additional 2,000 kilos of germanium would also be up for sale in the current fiscal year.
The Defense Dept has authorised the additional amount, but Congress has until April to object before the material can be made available, Connelly said.
The DNSC has chosen to use the sealed bid process to sell the material whereby all the names of the bidders and the prices they offered are published before any award is made.
Bidders in March can offer to buy a minimum of one box or 16 to 17 kilos or up to a maximum of 4,000 kilos.

The metal, which can be inspected at the stockpile's Hammond, IN depot between March 3 and 21, was acquired by the government in 1988-1990. It is in the form of zone refined polycrystalline ingot, produced by Metaleurop of France, Eagle Picher of the U.S., and Metallurgie Hoboken Overpelt of Belgium.

The stockpile is to begin selling some ten new commodities, including germanium, over the next ten years. At present some 40,000 kilos of germanium will be sold in maximum amounts of 4,000 kilos a year although Connelly said it was expected that this and next fiscal years' totals will be 6,000 kilos a year due to the amendment agreed earlier this month by the Defense Dept.
Germanium is usually a by product of zinc production, and used in high technology applications such as infrared, optical equipment and PET plastics used in packaging.
